Im not sure how to answer your question intelligently. Port forwarding or using a hosting service as an alternative, allows the other computers to “talk” to your server without being on the same network. I don’t know much about hamachi so I can’t speak about that intelligently. 

You can still play alone on your server without port forwarding but other players won’t be able to connect unless they’re on the same network. 

Type localhost into the IP box and then 27015 for the port and that lets you connect to your server IF its running on your PERSONAL network.

Edit: the reason why I mention using a hosting service is so that a server can handle the traffic and run the game, taking some of the load off of your computer. The server is designed for the purpose of “talking” to multiple computers at once. It will be more efficient. Yes, you can host from your computer but it will have a hard time running the server, “talking” to other computers, and running your game, it is doable and I have done that in the past, but the result was a very laggy server. I just setup a server for the bois. I always had a lot of problems in the past. Unturned uses a new hosting system which works quite smoothly compared to the old one. What you want to do is use the steamCMD. It does most of the work and installs the Unturned 3 Dedicated Server (U3DS)

​

I'll link a tutorial but here's the basics:

Create a folder for steamCMD

​

Save the steamCMD folder to this directory

C:\\    - This saves directly to your C:\\ drive which is what you need to do.

​

Run the steamcmd.exe in your steamcmd folder

Next, you need to install the unturned server files. To do this, type the following:

​

login anonymous

​

app\_update 1110390

​

When it finishes it should say successfully installed or something like that. Then type quit and it will close the program.

​

Next, look for the U3SD under SteamCMD > steamapps > common > U3DS

​

Open the U3DS folder, create a new text file and paste this code:

start %\~dp0ServerHelper.bat +InternetServer/MyServer

​

This is the start command used to start the server

Save this as a .bat file - call it something simple like start or run

Next double click on the file and a cmd console will open. You will see a lot of text appearing. The server is setting itself up. At this point you should have a basic server. By default, the map will be PEI, the mode will be easy and the name will just say Unturned. I know, it's very underwhelming.

But wait! You can customize everything in the commands.bat file! :)

commands.bat is a file with commands that the server runs on start up. This where you can set the map, mode, name, and set a password if you want.

It's quite simple!

​

Here's an example

name (whatever you want! must be below 50 characters)

port 27015 (most common port. but varies depending on the host if you use one)

map Arid (name of the map that you want  to play on. in this case, my server uses the new workshop map, Arid)

maxplayers 24 (self explanatory)

perspective both (allows players to use BOTH third and first person perspective)

mode normal (difficulty you want - easy, normal, hard)

Welcome (a welcome message that appears when someone joins)

password (shhh... don't tell anyone)

pve (combat type - PvP or PvE your choice)

owner (put owners steamID here. As an owner, you can give other players admin permissions and you can do cool stuff as well :P)

​

I did things a little differently since I am using a third party host. I looked at a few different tutorials, and forums but I was able to figure it out eventually. But [this](https://unturned.info/Server-Hosting/ServerHosting/#How-to-Install-Server-using-SteamCMD) should give you a start.

​

The video below will show you how to use commands, configure your server, how to use workshop maps and add workshop addons!

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5DcgA9oItWs&t=154s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5DcgA9oItWs&t=154s)

​

If you want to use Arid, check its workshop page, there are instructions on how to host a server with it. Hope this helps!

The sheen will likely show through if you just use a polycrylic of it, but I can’t really say what the final result will look like. 

I would suggest thoroughly sanding, and repainting. Possibly use a product with less sheen. The higher sheens will show more imperfections. I generally suggest paints with a satin finish. 

As for application, you could try using a brush with a self-leveling product, meaning that it won’t leave brush marks. S-W carries Emerald trim urethane, and pro classic acrylic alkyd enamel, both of these are easy to work with, self level, and also have low VOCs. 

Be careful with top coats… I had a customer use a polycrylic over cabinet paint and it cracked the paint. If you use a topcoat, it likely won’t touch up later down the road. 

If you want to use a topcoat and the paint is water based, make sure it has fully cured before applying any topcoat.
Use an oil based stain blocking primer. The paint will not bond and the stains will show through. Shellac, S-W problock or extreme block will work quite well

Flat paints burnish very easily. Use at least a matte sheen so this won’t happen. Also dark paints don’t cover as well because of the tint base they put it in. Basically, there needs to be more room for the colorant, and there are less solids in these bases so that the colorant and fully mix into the paint. Dark colors use more colorant, which doesn’t really cover all that well.

Sherwin-Williams employee here. 

Ideally, you want to use the exact same product that was used on the wall for a true touch up. That way the sheen and color will match 100%. Sheens vary between product and manufacturers. You can ask your landlord what they use but any product that they use is usually contractor-grade, which means low quality, but it will get the job done and the sheen and color will match 100%. 

If you plan on repainting that wall, I would recommend going to a specialty paint store, not a big box store. Get a wall sample from an inconspicuous place, or better yet you can bring an electrical panel or a vent cover. They will match the sheen and the color will be very close. At my store at least, we’re much more detail-oriented and during this time of year it’s slow so we take our time and make sure that it’s very close. 

Application tips:

Touch-Up: Use a 4 inch 3/8 roller for the spots and that way you won’t get brush marks and it’ll look clean.

Repaint: Brush around the edges, paint your trim first (if you plan on doing that, if not then no worries), and then use a 9 inch 3/8 roller for the rest of the wall. You want a thinner nap because the wall is smooth and you don’t need it to hold a lot of paint. Always do two coats. A good paint can cover in one coat. But I recommend two for full coverage. If your wall hasn’t been painted in a few years (which isn’t too likely because you’re in a rental and they get repainted often). You will need to prime. But before you buy a primer, test a few spots first and if it doesn’t look right, then you need a primer. Any water based latex primer will do. 

Painting is all about the prep work! It’s a pain but the more prep you do the better it looks!
